key_insight: High-speed video can be turned into physics-constrained molten-pool surface flow maps by combining optical flow with PINNs, even under noisy arc-lit conditions.
engineering_relevance: The approach can improve wire-arc DED process monitoring by linking visible surface motion to bead geometry, defect risk, and solidification behavior.
method: Homography-correct oblique high-speed video to obtain a calibrated top-view.
Extract dense optical flow as raw velocity observations.
Use a PINN to enforce Navier-Stokes consistency, boundary constraints, and arc-forcing priors; extend to a phase-conditioned time-dependent PINN for droplet-impact cycles.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reconstruction on high-speed imaging data from a GTAW-based wire-arc DED process across two flow regimes: quasi-steady convection and periodic droplet impact.
watch_item: Performance may depend on accurate camera calibration, reliable optical-flow estimates, and the validity of the imposed physics priors under changing melt-pool conditions.
paper_title: Reconstruction of Molten Pool Flow Fields from High-Speed Video Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
